'''Edzard Hans Wilhelm Reuter''' (16 February 1928 – 27 October 2024) was a German businessman. He was the [[CEO]] of [[Daimler-Benz]] from 1987 to 1995.

==Early life==
Edzard Reuter was born in Berlin on 15 February 1928. His father was the popular [[social democratic]] politician and later [[mayor of Berlin]], from 1948 to 1953, [[Ernst Reuter]].<ref name="o505">{{cite web | title=Ehemaliger Daimler-Benz-Chef Edzard Reuter ist tot | website=[[Deutschlandfunk]] | date=30 October 2024 | url=https://www.deutschlandfunk.de/ehemaliger-daimler-benz-chef-edzard-reuter-ist-tot-100.html | language=de | access-date=30 October 2024}}</ref><ref name="Trenkamp" /> His mother Hanna Reuter ''née'' Kleinert was a secretary at the party newspaper ''[[Vorwärts]]''.<ref name="Dettmer-2024">{{cite web | last=Dettmer | first=Markus | title=Edzard Reuter: Der Visionär, der Verluste hinterließ | website=[[Der Spiegel]] | date=29 October 2024 | url=https://www.spiegel.de/wirtschaft/edzard-reuter-der-visionaer-der-verluste-hinterliess-a-453a468f-1744-432c-8a94-2b7ee3518dda | language=de | access-date=30 October 2024}}</ref><ref name="tagesschau.de-2024">{{cite web | title=Ex-Daimler-Chef Reuter tot: Sozialdemokrat mit kostspieligen Visionen | website=tagesschau.de | date=29 October 2024 | url=https://www.tagesschau.de/inland/regional/badenwuerttemberg/nachruf-reuter-daimler-100.html | language=de | access-date=30 October 2024}}</ref> Under the Nazi regime, the family was forced to flee Germany; they found [[exile]] in Ankara, Turkey, where Reuter spent his childhood and youth.<ref name="Abgeordnetenhaus Berlin-2021">{{cite web | title=Edzard Reuter | website=Abgeordnetenhaus Berlin | date=26 March 2021 | url=https://www.parlament-berlin.de/Das-Haus/Berliner-Ehrenbuerger/edzard-reuter | language=de | access-date=30 October 2024}}</ref> In 1946, Reuter joined the [[Social Democratic Party of Germany]] (SPD).<ref name="Dettmer-2024" />

After returning to Germany in 1946,<ref name="m440">{{cite web | title=Berliner Ehrenbürger: Wegner: "Berlin trauert um Edzard Reuter" | website=[[Der Tagesspiegel]] | date=29 October 2024 | url=https://www.tagesspiegel.de/berlin/berliner-ehrenburger-wegner-berlin-trauert-um-edzard-reuter-12610574.html | language=de | access-date=30 October 2024}}</ref> Reuter studied [[mathematics]] and [[theoretical physics]] at the [[University of Berlin]], now known as [[Humboldt University of Berlin]], but then in East Berlin.<ref name="Trenkamp" /> He transferred to the [[Georg August University of Göttingen]].<ref name="Trenkamp" /><ref name="Berlin-Brandenburgische Akademie der Wissenschaften">{{cite web | title=Edzard Reuter | website=Berlin-Brandenburgische Akademie der Wissenschaften | url=https://www.bbaw.de/die-akademie/akademie-historische-aspekte/mitglieder-historisch/historisches-mitglied-edzard-reuter-3141 | language=de | access-date=30 October 2024}}</ref> In 1949, he switched over to studying [[law]] at the newly founded [[Free University of Berlin]].<ref name="Trenkamp">{{cite web |last=Trenkamp | first=Oliver | title=Ein Student und eine Universität im Aufbruch | website=[[Freie Universität Berlin]] | date=30 October 2024 | url=https://www.fu-berlin.de/presse/publikationen/tsp/archiv/2008/ts_20080419/ts_200800419_61/index.html | language=de | access-date=30 October 2024}}</ref> In 1955, Reuter completed his state examinations.<ref name="Trenkamp" /><ref name="Berlin-Brandenburgische Akademie der Wissenschaften" />

== Career ==
From 1954 to 1956, he was an assistant at the Free University.<ref name="Pillau" /> After applying for a job for Daimler-Benz and failing, possibly because of his political orientation,<ref name="Trenkamp" /> Edzard Reuter became an authorized signatory for [[Universum Film AG|UFA]], the German [[film studio]] and then an executive for [[Bertelsmann]], a media corporation.<ref name="Pillau" />

In 1964, [[Hanns Martin Schleyer]] recruited Reuter to work at the Daimler-Benz headquarters in [[Stuttgart]], where he advanced to the board of managers.<ref name="Pillau" /><ref name="tagesschau.de-2024" /> In July 1987, he succeeded {{ill|Werner Breitschwerdt|de}} as chairman of the board<ref name="Pillau" /> upon recommendation of [[Alfred Herrhausen]].<ref name="x072">{{cite web | title=Schwere Fehler | website=[[Der Spiegel]] | date=12 July 1987 | url=https://www.spiegel.de/wirtschaft/schwere-fehler-a-6f978d71-0002-0001-0000-000013523800 | language=de | access-date=30 October 2024}}</ref> Upon his assumption of office Reuter avowed himself to an "open" [[corporate culture]].<ref name="Dettmer-2024" /> His takeovers were the aircraft and defense technology of [[Dornier Flugzeugwerke|Dornier]], [[Messerschmitt-Bölkow-Blohm]] and [[MTU Friedrichshafen]], electronics from [[Matra]], and household appliances from [[AEG (German company)|AEG]].<ref name="tagesschau.de-2024" /> Daimler-Benz became a giant corporation, but it cost the company billions in losses.<ref name="tagesschau.de-2024" /><ref name="b970">{{cite web | title=Berliner Ehrenbürger Edzard Reuter ist tot | website=rbb24 | date=15 November 2016 | url=https://www.rbb24.de/panorama/beitrag/2024/10/edzard-reuter-gestorben-ernst-reuter-berlin.html | language=de | access-date=30 October 2024}}</ref> The way he exercised his functions was criticized by many including the economist {{ill|Ekkehard Wenger|de}}.<ref name="Dettmer-2024" /> In May 1995, Reuter was succeeded by [[Jürgen E. Schrempp]], who gave up his predecessor's business philosophy choosing instead to emphasize [[shareholder value]].<ref name="x476">{{cite web | title=Ex-Daimler-Chef Edzard Reuter: Schatten der Vergangenheit | website=stuttgarter-zeitung.de | date=26 February 2020 | url=https://www.stuttgarter-zeitung.de/inhalt.ex-daimler-chef-edzard-reuter-schatten-der-vergangenheit.3f33db92-8175-4936-ab11-1d763c49b193.html | language=de | access-date=30 October 2024}}</ref>

In August 1994, Reuter mentioned himself as a possible candidate for mayor of Berlin, but none of the parties showed interest.<ref name="o650">{{cite web | title="Ich bin ansprechbar" | website=[[Der Spiegel]] | date=28 August 1994 | url=https://www.spiegel.de/politik/ich-bin-ansprechbar-a-843daa56-0002-0001-0000-000013684789?context=issue | language=de | access-date=30 October 2024}}</ref> In 1998, Reuter became an honorary citizen of Berlin, especially for his dedication for the expansion of the [[Potsdamer Platz]].<ref name="Abgeordnetenhaus Berlin-2021" /><ref name="i887">{{cite web | last=Appenzeller | first=Gerd | title=Edzard Reuter zum 90. Geburtstag: Der Mann, der den Potsdamer Platz schuf | website=[[Der Tagesspiegel]] | date=16 February 2018 | url=https://www.tagesspiegel.de/berlin/der-mann-der-den-potsdamer-platz-schuf-3926380.html | language=de | access-date=30 October 2024}}</ref>

==Death==
Reuter died in [[Stuttgart]], Germany, on 27 October 2024, at the age of 96.<ref name="Pillau" />
